QF.id: AIFM CIII Fee Structure and Fund Performance_31

question.text: Which metric is the PRIMARY performance measure used in GIPS-compliant reporting of open-ended Cat III AIF performance to investors?

explanation.text: The Logic: Time-Weighted Return (TWR) is the standard performance methodology used to report open-ended fund performance because it neutralises the effect of investor cash flows and isolates the manager's investment performance. For open-ended Cat III AIFs, which transact at NAV with continuous subscriptions and redemptions, TWR (alongside NAV/unit) is the metric used in industry performance reporting and is recognised under GIPS as the appropriate methodology for this fund type. The Trap: IRR and MOIC are cash-flow-weighted metrics typically used for closed-end private-equity-style funds (Cat I/II AIFs) where capital is drawn down and distributed over time. MWR captures an investor-specific return, not manager skill across the fund. These are not the standard primary metrics for open-ended Cat III reporting. Note: The cited NISM Series XIX-E workbook pages (156, 452) list GIPS calculation methodologies including Gross IRR, Net IRR, TWR, MWR, and valuation methodologies, but do not explicitly state that TWR is the primary open-ended Cat III performance metric. The "primary metric for open-ended Cat III reporting" framing above is general industry/GIPS-aligned practice rather than a workbook-page citation.
